releases.notes:
**New: tiered label/border decluttering by zoom** — the world map (and minimap) now progressively hides overlay layers as you zoom out, so the map stays readable instead of turning into a wall of text/lines: resource labels disappear first, then node border lines, then train station labels, then town labels. Nation labels are never hidden. Uses XaeroPlus's own zoom-dependent window size, so it's free — no new data or config needed.

Note: the exact zoom thresholds are initial estimates and haven't been tuned against live map data yet (map.aechronis.net's `world.json` endpoint was returning 403 during testing). If the drop-off points feel off in practice, they're easy to adjust in `AechronisRenderer.java`.

releases.notes:
Covers everything since v1.0.12.

**New: chunk-border relation coloring (F3+G)** — ported from Aechronis Essentials. Recolors chunk borders by relation to the chunk's owner (town/nation/ally/enemy/neutral), each color configurable. Reuses the mod's existing towns.json/world.json poll (extended with nation allies/enemies and a player→town map) rather than running a second data fetcher.

**New: auto `/t spawn` on respawn** — optional, off by default; also ported from Aechronis Essentials.

**New: Train Station Icon Size** — a config slider (default 1.0) to shrink the minecart icon on the minimap and world map. Applied live, no rejoin needed.

**Fix: occupied-state race on annexation** — `annexTerritory()` wasn't holding the same lock as the towns.json poll's protected-set logic, so a chat-driven liberation landing mid-poll could be clobbered by a stale snapshot, resurrecting an "occupied" diagonal on land that had just been liberated/annexed.

**Fix: train station labels/routes could go stale forever** — the render cache was keyed on list size, so a poll that changed a station's tier, banned flag, or position (or moved a route's endpoint) without changing the total count left the old label/route on screen indefinitely. Now keyed on a version counter that bumps on every trains.json load.

**Fix: world-map search box overlapped Xaero's coords HUD** — moved down slightly.

**Cleanup** — removed the dormant `AechronisWarCapture` forensics logger (it had already served its purpose diagnosing prior war-state bugs).

releases.notes:
Nation territory fills now show up on the world map and minimap again — without the severe lag the first version of this fix (v1.0.11) caused.

- **Fix: missing nation colors** — the live map currently ships every town with its own color but an empty top-level nations list (no player nations have formed yet). The mod only ever resolved a fill color through town -> nation -> nation color, so every town resolved to no nation and got skipped entirely, leaving both the world map and minimap uncolored even though per-town color data exists. Towns not in a real nation now fall back to their own configured color, so territory fills render correctly again. A town that later joins a real nation switches over to that nation's color automatically.
- **Fix: severe lag from nation fills** — the live map turned out to have nearly its entire territory already claimed (~1.5 million chunks across ~13,000 territories), which v1.0.11 colored in all at once. The nation-fill renderer rebuilt its entire highlight buffer on the render thread every ~2 seconds regardless of what was actually on screen, which was the lag source. It now renders only whatever's in the current minimap/world-map viewport, refreshed off the render thread, so cost stays proportional to what's visible rather than to total claimed territory — this holds up even as real player nations grow to cover large parts of the map.
- No other behavior changes.

releases.notes:
Train station icon now also shows on the world map, not just the minimap.

- **Train station world-map icon** — the minecart icon (previously minimap-only) now renders on the world map too, alongside the existing station label. Five earlier attempts at this drifted from the label during zoom; the fix was routing the icon through the same buffered-draw mechanism the text labels already use correctly, with its own explicit flush every frame instead of relying on an unrelated feature's flush to pick it up late.
- No other behavior changes — minimap rendering, config toggles, and everything else are untouched.
